fields.credentialKept: set — leave empty to keep it
row.name: Name
body.lead: Where this realm PUSHES a service account's rotated password: a secrets manager the new password is written to as a new version before its hash is committed here, so a failed push changes nothing. Each destination is an application entry declared for the Secret push destination family, holding its own write credential — sealed, and never shown again once set. A push never creates a secret: the secret must already exist, so the credential needs write on the named secrets and nothing more. A service account names a destination and a secret on its own page.
body.development: Development mode. A file destination is offered here and refused in product mode: a password written to this container's disk is not in a secrets manager.
body.none: No secret destination is registered in this realm.
body.testPush: A test push writes a canary — a random password nobody uses — to a secret kept for testing; the secret a service account rotates into is refused.
